newsitem.title: USA: EU offers U.S. review of poultry decontamination.
newsitem.headline: EU offers U.S. review of poultry decontamination.

text.p: The European Union has offered to do a scientific review of U.S. hygenic practices in meat and poultry processing sectors, and specifically target the use of decontamination in poultry plants, a senior EU official said Thursday.
Lars Haelgaard, head EU negotiator in continuing talks with Washington over meat import inspections, said the offer was made in an attempt to resolve the escalating dispute.
But Hoelgaard said the plan would only study the use of lactic acid and TSP in the decontamination process, and not of chlorine, which is widely used by the U.S. poultry industry.
Whether the United States will accept the proposal is uncertain at this time.
The U.S. poultry industry has been pushing hard to get the EU to recognize the safety of cholorination.
Bill Roenigk, senior vice president of the National Broiler Council, told reporters he was concerned about the omition of chlorine in the EU proposal.
"That's the unfortunate part," said Roenigk of the proposal.

Roenigk said that switching to lactic acid or TSP would be more costly and less effective than chlorine for the industry, and said that, if asked, he would recommend that chlorine be included in the EU study.
